reference_reasoning.proposition: 2Co- and 5Co-MBG keep an ordered mesoporous channel structure with pores ~4-5 nm [n8], while Co addition lowers mesoporosity, dropping surface area from 290 to 180 and 127 m2/g and pore volume from 0.30 to 0.19 and 0.15 cm3/g [n9]
reference_reasoning.assumption: the single low-angle XRD reflection together with the TEM channel/lattice imaging and the type IV hysteresis loop are taken as jointly diagnostic of a retained ordered mesoporous architecture across all three compositions, and the BET-derived surface area, pore volume and pore-size distribution are taken as reliable measures of how that mesoporosity changes with Co content [writer inference]
reference_reasoning.open: whether the reduced surface area, pore volume and pore diameter at higher Co content alter the ordered channel arrangement itself, or leave only pore filling/blocking effects, is not addressed by these observations [writer inference]
reference_reasoning.handoff: an ordered mesoporous channel structure with pores ~4-5 nm persists in 2Co- and 5Co-MBG [n8], but Co doping progressively lowers mesoporosity, reducing surface area from 290 to 180 and 127 m2/g and pore volume from 0.30 to 0.19 and 0.15 cm3/g [n9]

dependency.why: this step reads phase and pore-structure evidence (XRD, TEM, N2 physisorption) directly from panels F2, F4a, F4b, F3a, F3b without relying on any prior step's conclusion, so it stands alone as a material-characterization finding

observations: F5a shows Co2+ in the soak medium rising over 7 days, reaching ~20.8 mg/L for 5Co, ~16.9 mg/L for 2Co, and staying at 0 for 0Co [obs1]
F9 shows the HIF-1alpha band faint for MBG and 2Co-MBG but clearly stronger for 5Co-MBG, with equal alpha-tubulin loading controls [obs2]
F11a shows cumulative ampicillin release climbing from ~340 ug at 8 h to ~780 ug at 72 h and then plateauing near ~795 ug by 168 h [obs3]

reference_reasoning.proposition: Ranking the scaffolds by Co2+ release rate gives 5Co fastest and highest (~20.8 mg/L at 7 days), then 2Co (~16.9 mg/L), then 0Co (0 mg/L) [n11]; but step 1 found surface area and pore volume fall in the same order, 290->180->127 m2/g and 0.30->0.19->0.15 cm3/g from 0Co to 2Co to 5Co [n9], so the scaffold with the least mesoporous texture (5Co) is the one that releases most, meaning release rises as texture falls and must instead track Co content [n11]
reference_reasoning.assumption: the inference assumes that if pore volume and surface area were the controlling variable, release would scale with them so that the most mesoporous scaffold (0Co, highest surface area and pore volume) would show the fastest or largest ion release, making a texture-driven mechanism testable against the observed order [writer inference]
reference_reasoning.open: how Co2+ crossing the framework interacts with the residual mesopore channels, and whether HIF-1alpha induction (F9) scales quantitatively with the 2Co versus 5Co release levels rather than just showing a qualitative band difference, is not resolved here [writer inference]. Co content and mesoporous texture are not independent across these three scaffolds: adding Co both lowers surface area and supplies more Co to release, so the two candidate causes co-vary and this comparison cannot fully separate a dose effect from a texture effect -- it only rules out texture acting in the direction a texture-driven mechanism predicts [writer inference]
reference_reasoning.handoff: the released Co2+, set by Co content rather than texture, is carried forward as a hypoxia-mimetic signal raising HIF-1alpha and driving VEGF [n12], while the separate ampicillin release from 2Co-MBG plateauing near 72 h [n15] is linked to the lowered bacterial survival over 7 days [n16]

dependency.why: answering whether texture or Co content controls the release rate requires comparing the F5a ion-release order against the surface-area and pore-volume order from step 1; without that prior characterization there is nothing to test the texture hypothesis against

combining.proposition: Release rises as surface area and pore volume fall, so it is set by Co content and not by the mesoporous texture: the 5Co scaffold has the least surface area and releases the most.

note: MatMech supplies which stretches are causal; our graph supplies the content. Every verdict is model against model.

reasoning: Small-angle XRD shows a single low-angle reflection in all three patterns, at 2theta ~1.37 deg for MBG, ~1.47 deg for 2Co, and ~1.35 deg for 5Co, indicating a periodic mesostructure persists across compositions [obs1].
TEM confirms this with parallel channel stripes over ~200 nm and a regular pore lattice with period ~5-6 nm [obs2].
Together these establish that 2Co- and 5Co-MBG keep an ordered mesoporous channel structure with pores of about 4-5 nm [n8].
N2 isotherms of all three show a type IV hysteresis step at P/P0 ~0.45-0.6, consistent with retained mesoporosity [obs3].
N2 uptake at P/P0~1 falls with Co content, from ~8.7 mmol/g (0Co) to ~5.6 (2Co) to ~4.35 (5Co) [obs4].
Pore-size distribution peaks stay near ~5 nm for 0Co and 2Co (2Co lower amplitude) and shift to ~4.2 nm for 5Co [obs5].

Combined with surface area falling 290 to 180 to 127 m2/g and pore volume falling 0.30 to 0.19 to 0.15 cm3/g, this establishes that Co doping progressively lowers mesoporosity while the ordered channel architecture is preserved [n9].
Co2+ concentration in the medium rises over 7 days for the doped scaffolds, reaching ~8.9/17.9/20.8 mg/L for 5Co and ~4.7/10.5/16.9 mg/L for 2Co at 1/3/7 days, while 0Co stays at 0 [obs1].
This establishes that Co2+ release rate and cumulative amount are set by Co content, with 5Co-MBG releasing faster and more than 2Co-MBG [n11].
Ranking the scaffolds by this release rate places 5Co above 2Co above 0Co [writer inference].

If the mesoporous texture from step 1 controlled this release rate, the highest-surface-area, highest-pore-volume scaffold would be expected to release fastest, yet 5Co has the lowest surface area (127 m2/g) and smallest pore volume (0.15 cm3/g) of the three [writer inference from n9].
Since 5Co nonetheless releases Co2+ fastest, the release rate tracks Co content rather than the mesoporous texture, so texture is not the controlling factor [writer inference].
Western blot shows the HIF-1alpha band is faint for MBG and 2Co-MBG but clearly stronger for 5Co-MBG, with equal alpha-tubulin loading [obs2].
This establishes that released Co2+ acts as a hypoxia mimic, raising HIF-1alpha in BMSCs, which drives VEGF, and that this effect scales with Co2+ release rather than with pore texture [n12].
Separately, cumulative ampicillin release from 2Co-MBG reaches ~340 ug at 8h, ~670 at 24h, ~780 at 72h, and plateaus near ~795 ug at 168h [obs3].
This establishes that 2Co-MBG releases ampicillin over the first ~72 h, after which release plateaus [n15].
Relative bacterial survival with ampicillin-loaded scaffolds falls to ~105%, ~81%, ~52% at days 1, 3, 7, versus ~100% for blank and 110-118% for drug-free scaffolds [obs4].
This establishes that ampicillin-loaded 2Co-MBG lowers bacterial survival compared with blank and drug-free scaffolds [n16].

Taking the Co2+ release property (n11) and the texture-versus-release mismatch as given, the HIF-1alpha blot (faint for MBG/2Co-MBG, clearly stronger for 5Co-MBG, equal tubulin) shows dose-dependent activation of the hypoxia pathway [obs1].
This confirms the mechanism that released Co2+ acts as a hypoxia mimic, raising HIF-1alpha in BMSCs, which drives VEGF, linking the release property to a pro-angiogenic cellular response [n12].
The bacterial survival data (~105/81/52% at days 1/3/7 with scaffold+ampicillin versus 100% blank and 110-118% drug-free scaffolds) shows the antibacterial performance delivered in service [obs2].

This establishes that ampicillin-loaded 2Co-MBG lowers bacterial survival versus blank and drug-free scaffolds, so the scaffold concurrently delivers a hypoxia-mimicking angiogenic cue and antibacterial performance [n16].
end_to_end.why_weakest: Step 2 folds together two mechanistically separate release systems (Co2+ driving HIF-1alpha/VEGF versus ampicillin driving antibacterial killing) with no node linking them, and its central texture-versus-release comparison rests on writer inference from combining n9 and n11 rather than on a stated node.
